mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; consular legalization if the country of origin is not a Hague Apostille Convention party

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, beneficial owners, and signatories against UN Security Council sanctions, EU consolidated financial sanctions, OFAC SDN and sectoral sanctions for any US-dollar exposure, French domestic asset-freeze lists, and GAFI/FATF high-risk jurisdiction indicators. PEP, family members, and close associates must be identified under Article L.561-10 of the Code monetaire et financier and the French AMF/ACPR guidelines. Enhanced due diligence is required where the SAS uses cash-on-delivery settlement in an elevated-risk emerging-market corridor, including source-of-wealth analysis, transactional liquidity checks, and submission of a suspicious activity report to TRACFIN where the beneficial owner cannot be verified or adverse screening results are unresolved.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalites des entreprises at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr and RCS availability verification through Infogreffe
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All statutory filings must be in French. The corporate name may contain reference to a foreign language but must be written in Latin script or transliterated into Latin script for insertion in the French commercial register. Accents commonly used in French are permitted. The selected name must not be identical, confusingly similar, or misleadingly similar to an existing French trademark, trade name, or registered company name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the registry refuses the name reservation or the incorporation filing, the application may be corrected and resubmitted through the Guichet unique. An administrative appeal may be filed directly with the Greffe du Tribunal de commerce in the jurisdiction of the intended registered office, and further judicial recourse may be brought before the President of the Tribunal de commerce in interim proceedings or before the Cour d'appel in the correctional chamber for refusal grounds related to available name and public order. The formal rejection notice must state the precise statutory ground, and the applicant has the right to request a written confirmation of the refusal to support a court challenge.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Limited permissibility. A domiciliation commerciale service provider with a valid contract and an authorized registered address may be used for an SAS, but a pure mail-forwarding virtual office or a telephone-answering mailbox is not acceptable for an SAS receiving cash-on-delivery remittances. Home domiciliation is permitted only temporarily and is commercially unsuitable for COD e-commerce due to the requirement for verifiable physical administration and receipt of regulatory correspondence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 30% within the first year where a commercial domiciliation provider is used and the SAS handles COD settlement in an enhanced-risk emerging-market corridor; the probability rises to approximately 55% over a three-year horizon if the registered office has no visible administrative substance, no local accounting records, or no supporting contract for the chargeable cash-on-delivery logistics activities.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L. 227-1 to L. 227-20 and R. 123-1 et seq.; applicable company-law provisions also appear in the Civil Code and the Monetary and Financial Code.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The competent local commercial court registry (greffe du tribunal de commerce), which maintains the Trade and Companies Register (Registre du commerce et des sociétés, RCS); filings are submitted through the INPI-operated Single Window (Guichet unique des formalités d’entreprises).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic company-creation formalité submitted through the INPI Single Window for registration in the RCS, including the required beneficial-ownership declaration.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital above EUR 1 applies to a SAS. At least 50% of cash contributions must be paid upon subscription; the balance must be paid within five years after registration. Cash contributions are deposited with an authorized bank, notary, or other permitted depositary, which issues a deposit certificate. The funds are released after RCS registration. Contributions in kind are generally subject to a contribution auditor unless a statutory exemption applies. The USD filing-fee figure is an indicative conversion of French-euro registry charges; actual charges vary and should be confirmed at filing.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The undersigned, being the duly appointed officers of [Company Name] SAS, resolve that the Company accepts the subscriptions set out in its executed Articles of Association and that the subscribed share capital is acknowledged as paid to the extent evidenced by the deposit certificate. The registered office is established at [full French address]. [Name] is appointed President for an indefinite term, with authority to represent the Company within the limits of law and the Articles. [Name] is appointed [additional office, if applicable]. The officers are authorized to complete registration, beneficial-ownership declarations, bank formalities, and all related filings. These resolutions take effect upon signature.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and execute the Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company founders; no filing authority is involved at this preparation stage.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the SAS Articles in French, specifying the company name, purpose, registered office, duration, share capital, share allocation, governance rules, President, and any additional officers. Obtain founder signatures. Use a qualified French translation for supporting foreign-language documents where required; arrange legalization or apostille when applicable.
required_dossiers: Draft and executed Articles of Association
Founder identity and address evidence
Corporate founder registration and authority documents, if applicable
French registered-office evidence
Appointment acceptance and non-disqualification declarations for officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct inconsistencies with identity records, registered-office evidence, capital terms, or mandatory statutory provisions; execute corrected Articles and replacement appointment documents before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: An authorized French bank, notary, or other legally permitted capital depositary.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary capital-deposit account, transfer the subscribed cash contributions, and obtain the deposit certificate for the registration filing. Ensure the deposited amount meets the statutory 50% initial-payment requirement for cash shares. Retain evidence of in-kind contributions and any required contribution-auditor report.
required_dossiers: Executed Articles or draft Articles accepted by the depositary
Founder and beneficial-owner identification documents
Subscription schedule and proof of transfers
Contribution-auditor report or documented basis for a statutory exemption, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Resolve depositary KYC queries with certified identity, ownership, source-of-funds, and corporate-authority evidence; correct transfer shortfalls and obtain an updated deposit certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A newspaper or online press service authorized to publish legal notices in the department of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish the required formation notice after the Articles are executed. Check that the notice accurately states the company name, legal form, capital, registered office, corporate purpose, duration, President, and RCS registration location. Obtain the publication certificate for the filing.
required_dossiers: Company formation particulars
Executed Articles or approved final company details
Publication certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request a corrected notice and certificate if any required company detail is incomplete or inconsistent with the Articles.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit the company-creation filing and beneficial-ownership declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Single Window (Guichet unique des formalités d’entreprises), with review and RCS registration by the competent local commercial court registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the electronic company-creation formalité through the INPI portal. Upload the signed Articles, registered-office evidence, capital deposit certificate, legal-notice publication certificate, officer appointment and acceptance documents, identity and non-disqualification declarations, and required beneficial-ownership information. Pay the portal-assessed charges and monitor the filing for requests for correction.
required_dossiers: Signed Articles of Association
Registered-office evidence
Capital deposit certificate
Legal-notice publication certificate
President and officer identity, acceptance, and non-disqualification documents
Beneficial-ownership information and supporting ownership documents
Founder authority documents, where a legal entity is a founder
Required translations and legalization or apostille documents, where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond through the INPI portal within the stated deadline, provide requested evidence, and correct or replace defective documents. If registration is refused, address the registry’s stated grounds and resubmit; use available review or appeal procedures where appropriate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Single Window, the competent RCS registry, the relevant tax authorities, and the company’s depositary bank.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain and verify the Kbis extract and SIREN/SIRET identifiers. Provide the registration evidence to the depositary to release the capital. Register for applicable tax and social-security obligations before commencing relevant activities, maintain statutory accounting and corporate records, and update the RCS and beneficial-ownership information when changes occur.
required_dossiers: RCS registration evidence or Kbis extract
SIREN/SIRET identifiers
Capital release instructions
Tax and social-security registration information, as applicable
Corporate registers and accounting records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct registry or tax-account data through the competent portal or authority; provide the Kbis extract and supporting documents to resolve depositary release or onboarding issues.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable to ordinary mail-order or e-commerce retail without a regulated industrial facility. The relevant local authorities may impose separate requirements if the company operates premises, stores regulated goods, or conducts activities subject to specific controls.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No general manufacturing or industrial operating permit is required solely for ordinary e-commerce retail. Separate activity-specific permits may apply to regulated products or services.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: French Ministry for Ecological Transition and Territorial Cohesion; the competent regional or departmental environmental authorities assess regulated projects where required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not applicable to ordinary e-commerce retail without a listed project or regulated installation. An environmental assessment or authorization may be required if the company later undertakes a project covered by the Environmental Code or operates an ICPE-classified installation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industry-specific wastewater, VOC, or industrial-waste thresholds arise solely from e-commerce retail. Any premises must comply with applicable municipal wastewater connection rules, general waste-management requirements, packaging extended-producer-responsibility obligations where applicable, and any permit conditions for regulated installations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No industrial fire, structural-load, or workplace clearance is required solely for an office-based e-commerce business. Customer-accessible premises may be subject to rules for establishments open to the public (ERP), including fire-safety and accessibility requirements; warehouses, workplaces, and installations must comply with applicable building, occupational health and safety, fire-protection, and insurer requirements.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), Ministry of Economy and Finance; online portals: impots.gouv.fr and formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; EU VAT validation via VIES.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a French SAS, the SIREN/SIRET registration is automatic upon incorporation through the Guichet Unique; the VAT intra-community number (TVA) is delivered by DGFiP to the local Entreprise Tax Office and must be shown on all invoices. A foreign entity holding French taxable operations must first appoint a tax representative established in France, then file an application with the DGFiP office (non-resident taxpayer unit) using an available French VAT registration form, together with evidence and a copy of the foreign registration document; the DGFiP issues a French VAT number, and the foreign entity remains subject to the same reporting obligations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists in France. The SAS is per se subject to corporate income tax under Article 206(1) CGI. Available elections include: (i) régime de l'intégration fiscale (group tax consolidation) for French subsidiaries held at least 95%; (ii) VAT grouping election (assujettis uniques) for entities under common control; (iii) election for the option taxable on dividend income under the parent-subsidiary regime; and (iv) anti-hybrid rules, including ATAD-aligned provisions, may require alignment of entity character with the jurisdiction of incorporation, without any elective hybrid conversion.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For a French-established business, there is no general threshold; any person making regular taxable supplies is obliged to register and obtain a VAT number. A small business exemption (franchise en base de TVA) applies where annual taxable turnover remains below EUR 91,900 for sales of goods and EUR 39,100 for services (2025 limits), except that e-commerce distance sales and cash-on-delivery retail channels are not automatically covered where the seller is established abroad; non-EU foreign sellers must register from the first transaction.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is rolling out mandatory e-invoicing for all VAT-registered B2B transactions through the Portail Public de Facturation (PPF) or an approved Dématérialisation Partenaire (PDP) platform from 1 September 2026 for large enterprises and 1 September 2027 for SMEs; e-reporting of transaction data to DGFiP is mandatory. Invoices must include a digital signature, QR code or an approved fiscal encryption, and all issued invoices must be transmitted in structured XML or Factur-X format. Real-time fiscal clearance at the time of each B2B sale is implemented through PPF; for B2C mail-order sales, the transaction data is reported at the same cadence and must preserve the full audit trail.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods outside the European Union qualify for VAT at 0% (exonération à l'exportation) where tangible property is dispatched or transported outside the EU, demonstrated by an electronic customs export declaration (mention 'exportation', code 00) and supporting transport documents. Purely offshore services to non-EU clients may be qualified as zero-rated under the French territoriality provisions of Article 259 CGI; the supplier must retain contractual evidence and proof of place of establishment of the recipient. Sellers must hold the export documentation within the second month following the sale to maintain the zero rate.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration en Douane / CPD)
Bill of Lading (Maritime, Airwaybill, or CMR international consignment note)
Commercial Invoice with incoterms and valuation
Evidence of dispatch from France or another EU state outside the EU
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank receipt proving payment from the non-EU buyer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The French tax administration may reverse the zero rating and reclaim VAT plus statutory accruals where the export evidence is incomplete, incorrectly reported, or where a fraudulent export arrangement is found. Penalties under Article 1729 CGI amount to 40% of the evaded VAT for bad-faith inaccuracies and 80% for manoeuvres frauduleuses (fraudulent schemes); delay interest accrues at 0.20% per month. Convictions may also carry criminal fines up to EUR 500,000 and prison sentences for tax fraud, and customs penalties for false customs declarations are imposed under the Code des Douanes. Export VAT refunds claimed without legally valid proof are treated as unjustified VAT recoveries and clawed back through a formal assessment procedure.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (BdF) as national central bank; European Central Bank (ECB) for monetary policy and eurozone FX operations
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Euro is fully convertible for both current and capital account transactions under EU capital movement liberalization (Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, Art. 63). No exchange controls or approval requirements for profit remittance, dividends, or repatriation of capital. However, all cross-border transfers exceeding €10,000 must be reported to the French customs and tax authorities for statistical and anti-money laundering (AML) purposes. Profit remittance is subject to standard corporate income tax (25% standard rate) and withholding tax on dividends (30% flat rate unless reduced by tax treaty). No restrictions on conversion of EUR to foreign currency for legitimate business purposes.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender or conversion of export proceeds into EUR. French law (Code Monétaire et Financier) does not impose any requirement to repatriate or convert foreign currency earnings. However, all export transactions must be declared to the Banque de France for balance of payments statistics via the 'Déclaration de Transaction' (DT) system if the transaction value exceeds €12,500. The declaration is electronic and must be filed within 20 days of the transaction. No conversion ratio applies; exporters may retain foreign currency in accounts abroad or in France.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Airwallex is a viable option for cross-border payments and multi-currency accounts. It operates in France under the EU Payment Services Directive (PSD2) via an e-money license obtained from the French Prudential Supervision and Resolution Authority (ACPR) or through passporting from another EU member state. Airwallex can provide local IBANs in EUR and support COD settlement via local logistics partners. However, for capital escrow purposes (e.g., shareholder loans or equity injections), a traditional bank account is often required by investors or legal counsel. Fintech EMIs are generally rated 'Medium' for core treasury operations due to limited credit facilities and potential regulatory constraints on large-value transactions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not strictly mandatory for corporate account opening in France. Most tier-1 banks allow remote onboarding via video identification (e.g., via ACPR-approved video KYC solutions) and digital signature. However, for complex structures (e.g., non-resident shareholders, beneficial ownership chains), banks may require a physical meeting with the legal representative or a notarized power of attorney. For SAS entities with non-resident directors, a physical visit to a French branch or a video conference with a bank officer is typically sufficient. The final decision rests with the bank's compliance department.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk business model: Cash-on-Delivery (COD) e-commerce, which involves cash handling and potential money laundering exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a detailed business plan explaining the COD model, including logistics partner agreements, cash collection procedures, and reconciliation processes. Submit audited financial statements (if any), proof of registered office, and a clear organizational chart. Include AML/CFT internal policies, customer due diligence procedures, and a risk assessment report. Also provide contracts with payment service providers (e.g., Airwallex) and logistics companies to demonstrate traceability of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholders or directors (especially from emerging markets) triggering enhanced due diligence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide passport copies, proof of address, and professional references for all beneficial owners. Submit a corporate registry extract (Kbis) and a certificate of good standing from the home jurisdiction. Include a detailed source of funds declaration for initial capital injection, supported by bank statements and tax returns. If the shareholder is a corporate entity, provide its audited financials and a breakdown of its ownership structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border transactions to/from high-risk jurisdictions (e.g., COD emerging markets)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Maintain a transaction monitoring system that flags unusual patterns. Provide a list of target countries and explain the commercial rationale. Submit copies of trade contracts, invoices, and shipping documents. Implement a robust AML screening process for all counterparties. Obtain a legal opinion on the compliance of the business model with French and EU sanctions lists.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For equity injection or shareholder loans from non-resident shareholders, use SWIFT wire transfers with proper purpose codes. For equity: use purpose code 'S301' (Investment in equity capital) or 'S302' (Investment in mutual funds) under the IMF Balance of Payments Manual. For loans: use 'S310' (Other investment - loans). The transfer must be accompanied by a copy of the shareholder resolution and the bank may require a certificate of the transaction's economic substance. For amounts above €10,000, the bank will report to the Banque de France. Ensure the beneficiary account is a French IBAN (e.g., FR76...). The bank will verify the source of funds and may request a declaration of the transaction's purpose.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade settlements (e.g., paying suppliers in emerging markets), use SWIFT MT103 for direct wire transfers or Commercial Letters of Credit (LC) for documentary credit. MT103 is suitable for low-value, high-frequency payments; LC is recommended for high-value transactions to mitigate counterparty risk. For COD logistics remittances, use local payment rails via Airwallex or partner banks to settle with local logistics providers. Ensure all outbound payments are accompanied by appropriate purpose codes (e.g., 'S200' for goods trade, 'S300' for services). For payments to high-risk jurisdictions, additional due diligence and sanctions screening are required.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward contracts (plain vanilla FX forwards) with maturities up to 12 months, available from major French banks and Airwallex.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for currencies with limited convertibility (e.g., certain emerging market currencies) – permitted under French law, but subject to counterparty credit risk and regulatory reporting.

Currency swaps (FX swaps) for managing liquidity and hedging both principal and interest payments – allowed for corporate treasury operations, subject to ISDA documentation and collateral requirements.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements approval and filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Court Registry (Greffe du tribunal de commerce) via the guichet unique
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Approval within 6 months after financial year-end; filing within 1 month after approval, or 2 months for electronic filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court injunction and potential daily penalty; administrative fine generally up to EUR 1,500, or EUR 3,000 for repeat breaches; persistent non-filing may lead to registry enforcement or administrative strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return Form 2065 and related schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French Tax Administration (Direction générale des finances publiques)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after financial year-end, or by the second working day after 1 May for a 31 December year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing interest generally at 0.20% per month and a surcharge generally ranging from 10% to 80%, depending on the circumstances and notice status.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Court Registry through the guichet unique
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No routine annual confirmation; changes to beneficial ownership or control must generally be filed within 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal and corporate officer liability may apply, including fines; inaccurate or missing information can trigger registry refusal, enforcement, and restrictions on registry filings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual management report and shareholder approval resolutions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company records; financial statements are filed with the Commercial Court Registry where required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Prepared for the annual approval process and submitted to shareholders within the statutory approval timetable; SAS articles may prescribe additional procedures
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Potential director liability, court-ordered compliance, and sanctions for failure to prepare or approve accounts; publication is not generally required unless separately mandated.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor is generally mandatory for an SAS meeting at least 2 of 3 thresholds: EUR 5 million balance-sheet total, EUR 10 million net turnover, or 50 average employees. Additional group and control rules may trigger appointment.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP under the French Accounting Standards Authority (ANC). IFRS may apply to qualifying consolidated accounts and may be used in permitted circumstances, but is not the default framework for standalone SAS accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France has no general annual UBO confirmation filing for an SAS. The company must update the beneficial ownership declaration when relevant information changes, generally within 30 days, and must maintain accurate shareholder and control records.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of shareholders or individual securities accounts
Register of transfers and movements of securities
Register of shareholder and corporate decisions
Minutes and attendance records for shareholder decisions
Beneficial ownership documentation and filed declarations

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 2,500-10,000 per year for a small or medium-sized SAS, subject to transaction volume, group reporting, and audit complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard corporate income tax rate. Qualifying small and medium-sized companies may apply a 15% rate to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit if, among other conditions, annual turnover excluding VAT does not exceed EUR 10 million, fully paid-up share capital is held at least 75% by individuals or qualifying entities, and the applicable ownership conditions are met.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The principal general preferential rate is the 15% SME rate described above. France also provides incentive regimes and credits subject to specific eligibility conditions, including research and development tax credits and certain regional or innovation incentives. No incentive follows solely from being a SAS, foreign-owned, or engaged in e-commerce. Eligibility, limits, state-aid rules, and reporting requirements must be verified for each claim.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Not limited to five years: corporate tax losses generally carry forward indefinitely, subject to an annual deduction cap of EUR 1 million plus 50% of taxable profit exceeding EUR 1 million. The balance may generally be carried forward. Carryback is generally elective and limited to the preceding tax year, subject to a EUR 1 million cap.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD (corporate income tax return), with the applicable corporate tax package and annexes, filed electronically through the Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP) EDI-TDFC channel, generally via an authorized intermediary or compatible software. Corporate tax payments are made electronically through the professional account on impots.gouv.fr.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual income tax return; corporate tax instalments are generally paid quarterly, with the final balance settled separately. Certain qualifying companies may be exempt from instalments.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: File within three months after the end of the financial year. For a financial year ending on 31 December, the return is generally due by the second working day after 1 May of the following year. The final corporate tax balance is generally due by the 15th day of the fourth month following year-end; for a 31 December year-end, it is due by 15 May. Instalments are generally due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December for calendar-year taxpayers, subject to the applicable rules and exemptions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the SAS's legal name, SIREN, registered address, tax office details, activity, and financial-year opening and closing dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign shareholder does not change the SAS's French resident corporate filing obligation. Use the French company's own SIREN and registered details; do not substitute the shareholder's foreign tax number.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2065-SD, taxable result and tax calculation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the taxable result and corporate income tax due, applying accepted tax adjustments, available loss utilization, and any substantiated preferential rate or credit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include the French SAS's worldwide taxable profits under French rules, subject to applicable treaty and domestic-law relief for foreign-source income. Do not exclude profits merely because a foreign parent or platform is involved.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report distributions and other amounts required by the return, consistently with the accounts, shareholder decisions, and applicable withholding filings.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify distributions to foreign shareholders accurately and separately meet applicable withholding and reporting obligations; treaty relief is not automatic.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2050 and following, balance sheet and income statement
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Complete the applicable standard corporate tax package schedules for balance sheet, profit and loss, fixed assets, depreciation, provisions, and tax reconciliations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the SAS's French statutory accounts and tax adjustments. Maintain support for related-party balances, cross-border charges, inventory, and marketplace or logistics settlements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile accounting profit or loss to taxable profit, including non-deductible expenses, tax-exempt income, depreciation differences, and other tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply French deductibility and transfer-pricing rules to payments to non-residents. Retain contracts, evidence of services or rights, allocation keys, and proof of business purpose.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report available tax losses and amounts used, subject to the statutory utilization cap and applicable continuity rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign ownership alone does not create a separate loss pool, but changes in activity or ownership and tax-neutral restructuring rules may restrict loss use.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Electronically pay the annual balance after crediting qualifying instalments and credits, by the statutory balance deadline.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payment responsibility remains with the French SAS. A foreign shareholder or parent should not assume that foreign tax payments discharge the French company's liability.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Pay the required instalments electronically on the statutory quarterly dates, calculated under the applicable rules and based on prior-year tax where required.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Assess instalment liability at SAS level and document any exemption or reduced payment position.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Where the statutory conditions are met, disclose prescribed information on related-party transactions, transfer-pricing policies, and relevant financial data.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include reportable transactions with foreign associated enterprises. This summary is separate from, and does not replace, any required transfer-pricing documentation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or missing returns generally attract a 10% surcharge, potentially 40% after formal notice and 80% in specified cases such as concealed activity or abuse of rights, plus late-payment interest generally at 0.20% per month. Tax shortfalls may also attract penalties of 40% for deliberate failure and 80% for fraudulent conduct or specified abusive arrangements. Separate fixed penalties may apply to missing or incomplete transfer-pricing documentation or reporting. Amounts and relief depend on the facts, procedure, and applicable statutory provisions.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Generally 25% on dividends paid by a French company to a non-resident, subject to domestic exemptions and treaty relief. A reduced or zero rate may apply under an applicable tax treaty or the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive if all ownership, holding-period, beneficial-ownership, anti-abuse, and procedural conditions are met. Payments to residents of non-cooperative jurisdictions may be subject to a 75% rate, subject to statutory exceptions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, identify the recipient's residence, beneficial ownership, legal form, participation, and eligibility under the relevant France tax treaty or EU directive. Obtain a valid tax residence certificate from the recipient's competent foreign tax authority and complete the applicable French withholding-relief certificate or refund procedure, commonly using forms in the 5000 series as appropriate to the income and treaty. Submit the required documentation to the payer and, where required, the French tax authority within applicable deadlines. If relief at source is unavailable, withhold at the domestic rate and claim a refund using the prescribed forms. Retain evidence of entitlement and monitor anti-abuse and principal-purpose requirements.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: French-source royalties paid to non-residents are generally subject to 25% withholding, subject to treaty reductions, qualifying EU relief, and statutory exceptions; payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions may face a 75% rate subject to exceptions. Interest paid to non-residents is generally not subject to French withholding tax, but exceptions include certain payments to residents of non-cooperative jurisdictions, generally at 75% subject to statutory exceptions, and specific statutory cases. The applicable treaty may reduce or eliminate withholding where permitted. Domestic deductibility, interest limitation, beneficial ownership, and anti-abuse rules apply independently of withholding.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Generally EUR 150 million: French transfer-pricing documentation obligations apply to entities meeting the statutory turnover or gross-asset threshold, or belonging to a group meeting the relevant threshold, subject to the precise conditions in the Tax Code. The annual summary return (Form 2257-SD) has its own statutory scope and thresholds; confirm the applicable threshold and filing conditions for the relevant tax year.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not have a general UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations regime. French tax law nevertheless applies substance-over-form principles, anti-abuse rules, beneficial-ownership requirements, permanent-establishment principles, and transfer-pricing rules. Arrangements lacking genuine functions, assets, risks, decision-making, or commercial purpose may be challenged under applicable domestic law, treaties, or EU anti-abuse rules.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and fraudulent tax return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing sales or payment receipts, maintaining false books, knowingly understating taxable profit, fabricating expenses, or using sham transactions to evade tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax adjustments, late interest, and penalties that may reach 80% in specified cases. Criminal tax fraud may carry up to five years' imprisonment and a EUR 500,000 fine for an individual, increased in specified aggravated cases to seven years and EUR 3 million; statutory multipliers and additional consequences may apply to legal entities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who personally participates in fraud may face criminal prosecution and personal penalties. A director may also be held liable for tax debts under statutory conditions, including fraudulent conduct or serious and repeated tax non-compliance that makes collection impossible. Imprisonment is not automatic; travel restrictions require a separate legal basis or order.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Late, incomplete, or inaccurate corporate tax compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file Form 2065 or required schedules, failure to pay tax or instalments, or material misstatement of the tax result.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Generally a 10% filing surcharge, potentially 40% after formal notice and 80% in specified serious cases, plus late-payment interest generally at 0.20% per month; additional tax and specific filing penalties may apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The SAS is primarily liable. Personal director liability may arise under statutory conditions for fraudulent conduct or serious and repeated non-compliance that prevents collection, or under criminal law for personal participation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Pricing controlled transactions other than at arm's length, failing to maintain or provide required documentation, or submitting an incomplete or inaccurate annual summary where required.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Taxable-profit adjustments, interest, and penalties may apply. Failure to provide required documentation may trigger a penalty generally set at the greater of 0.5% of the amount of transactions for which information was not provided and 5% of the corresponding transfer-pricing adjustment, subject to a statutory minimum and maximum. The applicable rules and caps must be checked for the tax year and circumstances.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The company is primarily liable. Directors may face personal consequences for deliberate fraud or personal participation; ordinary documentation failure does not automatically pierce the corporate veil.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Undeclared French permanent establishment or mischaracterized e-commerce activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Conducting business through a fixed place, dependent agent, or other taxable presence in France while failing to register, file, or attribute profits properly; treating French operations or personnel as belonging solely to a foreign principal without factual support.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment of French corporate tax and related taxes, interest, surcharges, and potentially criminal penalties where fraud is established. Treaty outcomes depend on the relevant treaty and actual facts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Company liability is primary. Directors may be personally exposed for knowing participation in evasion or where statutory conditions for personal tax-debt liability are met.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Improper dividend, royalty, or interest withholding
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Applying a treaty rate without valid residence and entitlement evidence, failing to withhold or report, or routing payments through an intermediary lacking beneficial ownership or commercial substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The payer may be assessed for unpaid withholding, interest, and penalties. Treaty benefits may be denied under domestic anti-abuse rules, the applicable treaty, or the principal-purpose test where relevant.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The SAS remains responsible as withholding agent. Personal liability is not automatic but may arise from intentional evasion, personal criminal participation, or applicable statutory director-liability rules.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using an entity with no genuine commercial purpose or actual decision-making to obtain treaty benefits, conceal the beneficial owner, or misattribute profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Benefits may be denied and tax reassessed under applicable abuse-of-law, treaty, beneficial-ownership, or transfer-pricing rules, with interest and penalties; criminal sanctions require the relevant criminal elements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable where they knowingly participate in fraud or satisfy statutory conditions for liability. A shell characterization alone does not automatically pierce the corporate veil.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly handling criminal proceeds, disguising beneficial ownership or payment flows, or failing to meet an applicable regulated intermediary's customer-due-diligence requirements. An ordinary retailer is not automatically subject to every AML obligation imposed on regulated financial institutions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering is punishable under French criminal law by up to five years' imprisonment and a EUR 375,000 fine for an individual, with higher penalties in aggravated cases; legal entities may face statutory fines and additional sanctions. Separate offences and sanctions may apply to the underlying conduct.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individuals who knowingly commit or facilitate money laundering may be prosecuted personally. Corporate status does not shield a participating director; travel bans or other judicial measures are fact-specific and are not automatic.
